children: Nearly 400,000 Russian deaths have been linked to the war in Ukraine in leaked government records reviewed by Bloomberg News, offering a rare view of losses Moscow has largely kept secret.

For investors, the findings highlight the conflict’s mounting demands on Russia’s workforce and public finances. Pressure to replace troops could compound those strains, while prospects for a ceasefire remain relevant to sanctions, energy markets and European security spending.

image.alt: Note: Does not include 16 deaths prior to 2022 and 116 deaths without dates. Death counts begin on Feb. 24, 2022. Data for 2026 is incomplete and not included; later months in 2025 likely underreport due to delays in recording deaths. For 8,858 deaths, the recorded date of death fell after the date on the death certificate. In these cases, Bloomberg used the death date in the registry’s original version.

children: Bloomberg identified approximately 392,700 death certificates explicitly tied to the conflict between the February 2022 invasion and late August 2026. The records were among more than 11 million certificates obtained by the hacking groups Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow.

The tally likely understates fatalities because some soldiers remain missing or unidentified, while other deaths lack a clear connection to military service. Registration delays also make recent figures particularly incomplete.
Rosstat, Russia’s statistics agency, acknowledged cyberattacks around the time of the alleged breach but said it found no evidence that confidential databases had been compromised.

Bloomberg said it could not conclusively authenticate the database. However, its examination found no signs of fabrication, and the records broadly matched previously published official mortality statistics.

The data suggest the burden has increasingly spread to older recruits. War-related causes accounted for more than 16% of deaths among Russian men aged 50 to 59 in the first half of 2025, compared with less than 1% during the invasion’s opening months.

Poorer regions also suffered disproportionately. In several Siberian regions, roughly a third of deaths among men aged 18 to 49 were linked to the war through mid-2024, versus about a tenth in Moscow and St. Petersburg.
Recruitment needs could increase pressure for additional mobilization. Russia has offered enlistment bonuses, although some payments are being reduced amid financial constraints.

Russia, Ukraine and the United States are expected to hold talks in Abu Dhabi this week on a possible ceasefire. The leaked figures provide a measure of the war’s human cost but do not establish whether Moscow is closer to accepting an agreement.

title: Leaked records point to nearly 400,000 Russian war deaths in Ukraine
